title: FRInGe: Distribution-Space Integrated Gradients with Fisher–Rao Geometry
claim: Instead of interpolating in input space, follow a geodesic in output-distribution space and pull it back to a stable input path.
layout: 1 panel, two parallel paths top and bottom, dotted pullback links between them
description: A single wide panel on a purple landscape with an orange region at the right. At the top, a black arrow-and-tick path runs from p(x0) to a maximum-entropy reference q*, passing through waypoints labeled q1 and q_{k+1}. Short orange segments mark the gradient ∇xL at selected waypoints. At the bottom, a white curved path in input space runs from x0 to xT. Red dots mark x1 and xk along it. A yellow arrow v marks the first step. A thick lime-green arrow from p(x0) down to x1 carries the label (G(x0)+λI)^{-1}∇xL, the Fisher-preconditioned step. Pink dotted lines link input points to their predictions on the top path. The eye goes first to the green arrow, then to the two contrasting paths.
caption: FRInGe constructs a Fisher--Rao geodesic from the initial prediction to a maximum-entropy reference in predictive distribution space and computes an input trajectory whose predictions approximately track its waypoints.
abstract: Although gradient-based attribution methods are model-faithful and scalable, a prominent variant, Integrated Gradients (IG), suffers from high sensitivity to design choices, particularly in baseline selection, path formulation, and discretization, as well as gradient saturation. To address these limitations, we propose Fisher--Rao Integrated Gradients (FRInGe), which defines both the reference and integration paths in the predictive distribution space. FRInGe replaces input baselines with a maximum-entropy predictive reference and follows a Fisher--Rao geodesic on the probability simplex. The corresponding input-space trajectory is realized through the pullback Fisher metric and stabilized by Kullback--Leibler (KL) and Euclidean trust regions; attributions are obtained by integrating input gradients along this trajectory. We further derive FRInGe-B, a variant that binarizes the predictive probability distribution, removing the computationally expensive Fisher products of FRInGe. Across six ImageNet architectures, FRInGe most clearly improves Magnitude Aligned Scoring (MAS), while remaining competitive on perturbation area-under-the-curve (AUC) metrics and infidelity.
